reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through iterative refinement of inertial sensor data using positional feedback. Initially, inertial units provide dead-reckoned estimates of motion. These estimates are subject to drift over time. To mitigate this, positional units—tracked via external systems such as optical markers or GPS—are used to anchor the inertial data. The process begins with predicting positional trajectories from inertial data, which allows association of positional measurements with inertial units. Subsequently, these associations enable correction of inertial trajectories using positional data, yielding drift-free segmental motion. Joint center alignment ensures geometric consistency across body segments. This dual-loop architecture enables robust tracking even under partial sensor loss or environmental interference. Failure modes include misalignment of positional units, sensor drift exceeding correction thresholds, and incorrect association of measurements with inertial units.
